audit.species: both — mouse (Cooper 2009 PNAS; Keppel 2013 J Immunol; Ni 2012 JEM, all C57BL/6 background Rag1-/-, Rag2-/-gc-/-, CD45.1/CD45.2 congenics) and human (Romee 2012 Blood, apheresis-donor blood NK, in vitro only; Romee 2016 Sci Transl Med, healthy-donor NK in vitro + NSG xenograft + haploidentical donor NK in AML patients)
audit.what_was_measured: MOUSE (Cooper 2009, the term-coining paper): splenic NK cells negatively enriched from Rag1-/- donors (60-95% NK1.1+, or FACS-sorted >98%) were cultured in vitro for 13-15 h with IL-12 10 ng/mL + IL-18 50 ng/mL plus low-dose IL-15 10 ng/mL, or with IL-15 10 ng/mL alone (control); washed 4x, labelled with 1 uM CFSE (2.5 uM for the 22-day arm), and 1.5-3 x 10^6 cells injected i.v. into Rag1-/- hosts. At day 7 and day 22 the readout was % intracellular IFN-gamma by flow cytometry in CFSE+NK1.1+ (donor) versus CFSE-NK1.1+ (host) splenocytes after 4 h ex vivo IL-12+IL-15 or 8 h plate-bound anti-Ly49H / anti-NK1.1; plus CFSE-dilution generation gating, granzyme B ICS, and 4 h 51Cr-release killing of YAC-1. Donor identity rested entirely on a dilutable dye (CFSE), not a congenic allele. MOUSE (Keppel 2013): identical preactivation applied to CD45.1+ and CD45.2+ Rag1-/- NK cells that were CO-transferred into a single Rag1-/- or alymphoid Rag2-/-gc-/- host; %IFN-gamma after 4 h IL-12+IL-15 measured at days 1, 3, 7, 21 (to 4 wk alymphoid, 12 wk NK-competent). HUMAN in vitro (Romee 2012): RosetteSep-purified (>=95% CD56+CD3-) or FACS-sorted (>=99%) blood NK cells preactivated 16 h with rhIL-12 10 + rhIL-18 50 + rhIL-15 1 ng/mL versus rhIL-15 1 ng/mL control, rested 7/14/21 d in 1 ng/mL IL-15, restimulated with IL-12+IL-15, IL-12+IL-18 or K562, %IFN-gamma read by flow; CFSE 5 uM for division tracking; no in vivo arm. HUMAN in vivo (Romee 2016, phase 1): 13 enrolled / 9 evaluable AML patients received Flu/Cy (days -7 to -2), one infusion of haploidentical IL-12/15/18-preactivated donor NK cells, then 6 doses of sc rhIL-2 1x10^6 IU/m2; donor cells were identified in blood (d1,3,7,8,14,21,30,60,100) and marrow (d8,14,30,60,100) with donor- or patient-specific anti-HLA monoclonal antibodies by flow cytometry, reported as >90% of blood NK cells donor-derived at day 7 and a 419 +/- 166-fold day1-to-day7 increase.
audit.n: Cooper 2009: n=7 (in vivo proliferation, Fig 2A), n=4 (IFN-gamma after IL-12+IL-15, Fig 2D); phenotype panels "representative of 2-5 independent experiments"; Fig 4 generation analysis "mean of 3 independent experiments"; cytotoxicity 2 independent experiments, duplicate wells. Keppel 2013: "mean +/- SEM of 3-7 independent experiments" (Rag1-/- co-transfer), 4 independent experiments (Rag2-/-gc-/-). Ni 2012: n=3-8 per group. Romee 2016: 13 enrolled / 9 evaluable patients, 8 with informative HLA at all timepoints; NSG xenografts n=12-24 per group over 2-3 experiments; mass cytometry on 9 individuals. Romee 2012: donor number NOT stated in the Methods section.
audit.n_unit: animals (mice) for Cooper 2009 / Keppel 2013 / Ni 2012 and for the NSG xenografts; patients for the Romee 2016 phase 1 trial; donors (unstated number) for Romee 2012 human in vitro work. NOTE: Cooper 2009's n=7 and n=4 are recipient mice, not cells; Keppel 2013 reports only "independent experiments", not animals, so its true animal n is not recoverable from the paper.
audit.controls: Cooper 2009: (i) paired control NK cells given low-dose IL-15 alone and transferred into separate hosts; (ii) CFSE-negative endogenous host NK cells inside the same recipient as an internal control (used to show the effect was NK-intrinsic — "there was no difference in IFN-gamma production by host NK cells from mice that received previously-activated NK cells versus recipients of control NK cells"); (iii) FACS-sorted >97% pure NK cells repeated to exclude co-transferred APCs; (iv) granzyme B positive control (48 h 100 ng/mL IL-15) and isotype controls; (v) an explicit, single-marker test of the selection alternative — "we did not observe a preferential expansion of CD27hi NK cells". Keppel 2013 adds the strongest control in the literature: CD45.1/CD45.2 congenic CO-transfer of preactivated and control NK cells into ONE host, so both populations share an identical in vivo environment; plus Rag2-/-gc-/- hosts injected with CD45.1 activated NK alone to exclude de novo endogenous NK development (no CD45.1-negative NK out to 4 months). Ni 2012: CD45.1 congenic donors into CD45.2 recipients, IL-15-alone control cells, IL-2 neutralisation and CD4 depletion arms, irradiated vs non-irradiated hosts. Romee 2016 CLINICAL TRIAL: NO control arm — no non-preactivated donor NK comparator was infused, and the trial could not distinguish memory-like from conventional donor NK cells in vivo (anti-HLA mAbs resolve donor vs recipient only).
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: SELECTION OF A PRE-EXISTING HYPER-RESPONSIVE SUBSET RATHER THAN CONVERSION. Every experiment in this literature tracks a BULK population with a non-clonal label — a dilutable dye (CFSE, Cooper 2009), a congenic allele shared by millions of cells (CD45.1/CD45.2, Keppel 2013 / Ni 2012), or an HLA mismatch shared by the whole graft (Romee 2016). None of these can distinguish "each NK cell converted" from "the responsive minority survived, homed and expanded". Three independent lines make selection concrete: (1) IL-12/15/18 preactivation itself kills NK cells — Terren et al. 2023 Front Immunol (PMID 37575238) report that "upon IL-12/15/18 stimulation the viability of NK cells decreased", with raised mitochondrial superoxide and impaired mitophagy, so the preactivation step is itself a survival filter; (2) Romee 2012's own data map the memory-like IFN-gamma response onto markers that exist BEFORE preactivation — CD94, NKG2A, NKG2C and CD69 high with CD57 and KIR absent, i.e. the less-differentiated pre-existing compartment; Foltz et al. 2024 Sci Immunol (PMID 38941480) reach the same place by Waddington-OT/CellRank fate-probability inference (eML-1 from CD56bright, eML-2 from CD56dim) with NO barcoding and no lineage tracing; (3) in patients, Shapiro et al. 2022 JCI (PMID 35349491) found that "Patients 3 and 4 both exhibited a dominance of NK clusters on day +28 and day +60 that constituted a minor portion of the infusion product" — disproportionate outgrowth of a minor pre-existing subset, which is the selection model, and they state outright that "there was no traceable marker in the infused CIML NK cells, it was not possible to use donor chimerism or other direct means to track the infused NK cells." SECOND ALTERNATIVE — the recovered state is not "memory" but a persistently activated / homeostatically expanded effector state: Ni et al. 2012 JEM (PMID 23209317) used the same IL-12/15/18 cocktail with proper CD45.1 congenic tracking and found cells that persist >=3 months but are KLRG1-hi, granzyme B-hi and phenotypically mature, whose proliferation is IL-2- and CD4-T-cell-dependent and which require 5 Gy host irradiation to work — the opposite of Cooper's granzyme-B-negative, non-cytotoxic resting "memory" cell. Keppel 2013 saw KLRG1 rise on BOTH preactivated and control cells after homeostatic expansion and conceded in print that "these enhanced responses could represent a residual priming effect, rather than a memory-like response." THIRD ALTERNATIVE (human trial only) — lymphodepletion plus cytokine support, not preactivation, drives the in vivo expansion and the remissions.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, four named published counter-examples/alternatives, all read at methods level: (1) Ni J, Miller M, Stojanovic A, Garbi N, Cerwenka A, J Exp Med 2012;209:2351-2365, PMID 23209317 / PMC3526364 — same IL-12(10)/IL-15(10)/IL-18(50) cocktail, better tracking (CD45.1 congenic into CD45.2 B6), but the persisting cells are KLRG1-hi/granzyme-B-hi sustained EFFECTORS, expansion is IL-2- and CD4-T-cell-dependent and requires 5 Gy host irradiation; directly contradicts Cooper 2009's granzyme-B-negative, non-cytotoxic resting memory cell. (2) Miller JS et al., Blood 2005;105:3051-3057, PMID 15632206 — haploidentical NK cells activated overnight with IL-2 ONLY (no IL-12, no IL-18) after Hi-Cy/Flu plus sc IL-2 showed "marked rise in endogenous IL-15, expansion of donor NK cells, and induction of complete hematologic remission in 5 of 19" poor-prognosis AML patients; this reproduces Romee 2016's in vivo expansion and 4 CR / 9 evaluable outcome WITHOUT IL-12/15/18 preactivation, so the human in vivo result is not attributable to CIML differentiation. (3) Terren I et al., Front Immunol 2023;14:1211839, PMID 37575238 / PMC10413107 — IL-12/15/18 stimulation decreases human NK cell viability, establishing the preactivation step as a survival filter that can enrich rather than convert. (4) Shapiro RM et al., J Clin Invest 2022;132:e154334, PMID 35349491 / PMC9151697 — independent group, 6 patients; no traceable marker so the infused CIML NK cells could not be tracked at all, and minor infusion-product clusters dominated at day +28/+60 while the compartment "largely resembled that seen prior to infusion" by day +60. ALSO relevant as a weak-evidence flag rather than a contradiction: Foltz JA et al., Sci Immunol 2024;9:eadk4893, PMID 38941480 / PMC12329699 — the current mechanistic account of ML subset origin rests on Waddington-OT / CellRank trajectory inference with no clonal barcoding (INF_TRAJECTORY). SEARCHED AND NOT FOUND: no clonal barcoding, no genetic fate-mapping and no mitochondrial-variant clonal tracking study of CIML NK cells exists in mouse or human — I searched for it explicitly and found nothing.
audit.downstream_dependency: An entire adoptive-cell-therapy manufacturing platform treats "16 h IL-12/IL-15/IL-18 preactivation = a differentiated memory-like cell" as an established fact and builds products on it. Concrete named dependencies: (a) Romee 2016 Sci Transl Med phase 1 trial NCT01898793 in relapsed/refractory AML (4 CR of 9 evaluable) — the entire rationale is that the infused cells are a differentiated ML state, yet the trial itself could not distinguish ML from conventional donor NK cells in vivo; (b) Bednarski JJ et al., Blood 2022;139:1670-1683, PMID 34871371, pediatric post-transplant relapsed AML, which identifies "persisting ML NK cells" out to 3-6 months purely by viSNE clustering on CD56-hi/NKG2A/CD62L phenotype with no traceable marker — if the ML state is a selected pre-existing CD56bright-like subset, that entire persistence claim collapses into "a subset was expanded"; (c) Shapiro RM et al., J Clin Invest 2022, PMID 35349491; (d) the engineered CAR-ML-NK product line, which uses ML differentiation as a fixed manufacturing step: Gang M et al., Blood 2020;136:2308-2318, PMID 32614951 (CD19-CAR memory-like NK vs NK-resistant lymphoma); Dong H et al., PNAS 2022;119:e2122379119, PMID 35696582 (NPM1c-neoepitope CAR ML NK); mesothelin-CAR ML NK, Sci Adv 2024, PMID 38996027; (e) the 2025 first-in-human ML NK + IL-15 superagonist N-803 + CTLA-4 blockade trial in advanced head and neck cancer, PMID 39948608. If the operative mechanism is selection/expansion of a pre-existing responsive subset plus lymphodepletion-driven homeostatic expansion (Miller 2005) rather than induced memory differentiation, the correct manufacturing optimisation target changes from "how long/strong to preactivate" to "which pre-existing subset to sort and expand" — a different product.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: The CLASS in Claude's initial call survives — OBS_TRANSFER is genuinely present, and in mouse it is well executed. But four specific components of the initial call and its starting hints are WRONG or materially overstated, and I am changing them. (1) THE HINT'S PREMISE ABOUT CONGENIC MARKERS IN COOPER 2009 IS FALSE. Cooper 2009 used NO congenic marker. Donor identity was CFSE dye alone ("labeled with 1 uM CFSE ... transferred i.v. into Rag1-/- hosts. Donor-derived, CFSE+NK1.1+ NK cells were easily detected 1 to 3 weeks later"), and the authors concede the dye fails on dividing cells: "It is possible that we were unable to detect some NK cells due to proliferation and CFSE dilution, resulting in the inclusion of these cells among the host NK cell pool." Congenic CD45.1/CD45.2 co-transfer appears only later, in Keppel 2013 J Immunol and independently in Ni 2012 JEM — so the strongest transfer evidence is NOT the paper the hint points to. (2) THE COCKTAIL IS MISATTRIBUTED. Cooper 2009 did not use IL-12/IL-15/IL-18 as the memory-inducing triple; it used IL-12 + IL-18 with low-dose IL-15 explicitly as a survival factor, and showed IL-15 was DISPENSABLE ("NK cells preactivated with IL-12 + IL-18 with or without low-dose IL-15 for 5 h had an enhanced capacity to produce IFN-gamma"). The canonical IL-12/IL-15/IL-18 triple in the claim traces to Romee 2012 Blood (human, entirely in vitro) and Ni 2012 JEM (mouse). (3) "TRANSFER + PERSISTENCE" OVERSTATES THE HUMAN ARM. In Romee 2016 the anti-HLA mAb readout resolves donor vs recipient NK cells only — it does NOT distinguish memory-like from conventional donor NK cells in vivo, there was no non-preactivated donor NK control arm, and Miller 2005 Blood (PMID 15632206) already produced the same expansion and the same CR rate with IL-2-activated (non-CIML) haploidentical NK cells under the same Flu/Cy + IL-2 conditioning. The human in vivo evidence is therefore INF_MARKER for the "memory-like state", not OBS_TRANSFER. (4) NO CLONAL-RESOLUTION EVIDENCE EXISTS ANYWHERE. The conversion step itself is INF_INVITRO in every paper; the transfers establish PERSISTENCE and cell-intrinsic heritability of a bulk-population property, not that any individual resting NK cell became a CIML NK cell. Searched specifically for barcoding / genetic fate-mapping / mtDNA clonal tracking of CIML NK — none exists. Net revision: keep OBS_TRANSFER as strongest, but downgrade to "OBS_TRANSFER in mouse for persistence only; conversion step is INF_INVITRO; human in vivo claim is INF_MARKER", and flag that the selection alternative is unexcluded and has three lines of published support (Terren 2023, Romee 2012's own marker correlations, Shapiro 2022's minor-subset dominance).

audit.methods_quote: Cooper et al. 2009 PNAS, Materials and Methods, "NK Cell Isolation and Adoptive Transfer": "NK cells were activated with IL-12 (10 ng/mL, PeproTech), and IL-18 (50 ng/mL...) in the presence of low-dose IL-15 (10 ng/mL, PeproTech), or control-treated with IL-15 alone overnight (13-15 h)... The next day cells were harvested, washed a total of 4 times in PBS (PBS), and labeled with 1 uM CFSE (Invitrogen) or for 22 day experiments NK cells were labeled with 2.5 uM CFSE. Equal numbers of CFSE-labeled NK cells (~1.5-3 x 10^6) were adoptively transferred into Rag1-/- mice by tail vein injection." — this is what makes it OBS_TRANSFER, and equally what caps it: donor identity is a dilutable dye. The same paper's Discussion concedes the cap: "It is possible that we were unable to detect some NK cells due to proliferation and CFSE dilution, resulting in the inclusion of these cells among the host NK cell pool." Keppel et al. 2013 J Immunol, Materials and Methods, "Adoptive transfers", supplies the congenic version: "Splenocytes were obtained from Rag-1-/- donors (CD45.1 or CD45.2)... For co-transfers, equal numbers of cells (~1-3 x 10^6) were adoptively transferred by intravenous injection into the indicated hosts (Rag-1-/-, CD45.1+ Rag-/-, or Rag-2-/- gc-/-)." Contrast Romee et al. 2016 Sci Transl Med, which for the human in vivo arm supports only INF_MARKER: "Donor memory-like NK cells were tracked in the blood of all patients with informative HLA [using donor- or patient-specific anti-HLA monoclonal antibodies (mAbs)]" — donor vs recipient only, with no ML-vs-conventional discrimination and no non-preactivated donor NK control arm.

Verbatim full text I actually read is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aaa/5f46e874-56b9-5c6b-9d27-d08dbfb1d5d8/scratchpad/cooper2009.txt (Cooper 2009, complete Methods + Results + figure legends) and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aaa/5f46e874-56b9-5c6b-9d27-d08dbfb1d5d8/scratchpad/PMC3633638.txt (Keppel 2013, complete). TERMINOLOGY WARNING for the registry: "CIML NK" is a FUNCTIONAL STATE claim (enhanced recall IFN-gamma), not a lineage-conversion claim in the sense used for the other rows in this screen. Cooper 2009 explicitly shows the state does NOT include the usual differentiation correlates — the cells are granzyme B negative and kill YAC-1 no better than naive NK ("all 4 groups of NK cells exhibited similar cytotoxicity"), and are phenotypically indistinguishable from control NK on CD69, CD11b, CD11c, gp49B, B220, CD122, IL-15Ralpha, IL-12Rbeta1, CD127. So "A becomes B" here means "A acquires a heritable functional bias", and the only positive marker of B is the recall assay itself — which makes B unfalsifiably co-extensive with the assay used to define it. Two further methods-level caveats worth carrying: (i) Cooper 2009's memory-like effect is dose/duration dependent (5 h preactivation gives a weaker effect than overnight), consistent with a graded priming decay rather than a discrete state switch, and the authors themselves offer the alternative reading in print — "Alternatively, an increased activation time may allow for a higher percentage of NK cells to differentiate into memory-like cells"; (ii) the one genuinely strong anti-selection datum is Cooper 2009 Fig 4 — generation-0 (never-divided) preactivated cells make as much IFN-gamma as generations 1-3 — which excludes proliferation-linked epigenetic acquisition but does NOT exclude differential survival, the selection route that Terren 2023's viability data make live. Kinetic framing (day-1 "primed" vs day-7/21 "memory-like" in Keppel 2013) is INF_KINETIC and is doing real interpretive work in that paper.

adv.challenge_reason: I re-read Cooper 2009 (PMC2644138) Methods and Results verbatim and independently pulled Romee 2012 (PMC3520618) Methods; the auditor's factual reads are accurate, but the CLASS assignment is scoped wrong. OBS_TRANSFER is credited to something the transfer did not do. Spec definition: "A transferred, B recovered from the recipient." In this claim A = resting NK cell and the arrow = IL-12/IL-15/IL-18 preactivation. In EVERY paper, A was never transferred: Cooper 2009 Methods state NK cells were "activated with IL-12 (10 ng/mL)... and IL-18 (50 ng/mL)... in the presence of low-dose IL-15 (10 ng/mL)... overnight (13-15 h)", and Fig S1 shows ">90% of NK cells [produced] IFN-gamma protein... indicating that the vast majority of these cells were activated at the time of adoptive transfer." The generative step happened in a culture dish; the i.v. injection came afterwards. Romee 2012 makes this decisive: the paper that actually introduced the IL-12+IL-15+IL-18 TRIPLE named in the claim ("preactivated for 16 hours using rhIL-12 (10 ng/mL) + rhIL-18 (50 ng/mL) + rhIL-15 (1 ng/mL)") has NO in vivo arm at all — its own Discussion says "Currently, we are evaluating in vivo xenograft approaches in NOD-SCID-gc-/- mice." The entire human demonstration of the claimed conversion is a dish. Therefore the strongest class covering the CLAIMED ARROW is INF_INVITRO. OBS_TRANSFER is genuinely present and well executed (Keppel 2013 CD45.1/CD45.2 co-transfer; Ni 2012), but it licenses only a narrower proposition: that a bulk population carrying the recall-IFN-gamma property persists and transmits it cell-intrinsically in vivo. It never observes a cell convert. Two further methods facts the auditor noted but did not let bite the class: (i) Cooper 2009's donor label is CFSE, a dilutable dye, and the paper concedes "It is possible that we were unable to detect some NK cells due to proliferation and CFSE dilution"; (ii) B is defined solely by the ex vivo restimulation assay (4 h IL-12+IL-15, %IFN-gamma on a bulk gate) — a functional-marker readout, which is INF_MARKER machinery, not observation of conversion. NO UPGRADE is available: I searched specifically for CIML lineage tracing / fate mapping / mtDNA-variant clonal tracking / single-cell transfer (4 distinct PubMed queries) and got 0 hits each. Verdict: DOWNGRADE the recorded strongest class from OBS_TRANSFER to INF_INVITRO, retaining OBS_TRANSFER in evidence_types_all scoped to mouse persistence only. This promotes into the classification field what the auditor had already conceded in prose but declined to record.
adv.revised_evidence_type_strongest: INF_INVITRO (for the claimed conversion step: resting NK + IL-12/IL-15/IL-18 -> CIML NK, which occurs entirely in vitro in Cooper 2009, Romee 2012, Ni 2012, Romee 2016 and every manufacturing protocol). OBS_TRANSFER survives ONLY for the narrower proposition "the recall-IFN-gamma property persists and is cell-intrinsically heritable in a bulk mouse NK population" (Keppel 2013 CD45.1/CD45.2 congenic co-transfer into one host, PMID 23530145; Ni 2012 CD45.1->CD45.2, PMID 23209317). Human in vivo evidence is INF_MARKER only, and is WEAKER than the auditor recorded: Berrien-Elliott 2022 Sci Transl Med (PMID 35196021, PMC9210521) states verbatim "HLA-based NK cell tracking was not possible because the immune cells reconstituting after haplo-HCT are HLA-matched to the infused same-donor NK cells" — the flagship ">2 month persistence" claim rests on unsupervised mass-cytometry/CITE-seq clustering with zero donor tracking. Full list unchanged: INF_INVITRO, OBS_TRANSFER (scoped), INF_MARKER, INF_KINETIC, INF_TRAJECTORY (Foltz 2024 Waddington-OT/CellRank, PMID 38941480).
adv.new_counter_evidence:
SIX papers the auditor missed, all read at methods/results level; the first two are the most damaging and both come from the originating (Fehniger/WashU) lab.

(1) Leong JW, Chase JM, Romee R, Schneider SE, Sullivan RP, Cooper MA, Fehniger TA. "Preactivation with IL-12, IL-15, and IL-18 induces CD25 and a functional high-affinity IL-2 receptor on human cytokine-induced memory-like NK cells." Biol Blood Marrow Transplant 2014;20:463-473. PMID 24434782 / PMC3959288. 16 h preactivation induces CD25 on CD56dim and CD56bright NK, persisting >=7 days; CD56dim cells then "were induced to proliferate in a dose-dependent manner" at ">=10 pM" IL-2, abolished by anti-CD25 blocking antibody; and verbatim: "Following adoptive transfer into immunodeficient NOD-SCID-gc-/- mice, human cytokine pre-activated NK cells expand preferentially in response to exogenous IL-2," supporting that "low dose IL-2 therapy can support survival... of IL-12, IL-15, and IL-18 pre-activated allogeneic NK cells following adoptive transfer." This is a MECHANISTIC preferential-expansion/survival account of the very in vivo readout the claim leans on. Romee 2016 gave 6 doses of sc rhIL-2; its headline 419 +/- 166-fold day1-to-day7 donor NK expansion is therefore fully predicted by "preactivation installs a high-affinity IL-2R, then we gave IL-2" — a selection/expansion mechanism, no memory required. The auditor's selection alternative was generic; this makes it specific and same-lab.

(2) Berrien-Elliott MM et al. "Hematopoietic cell transplantation donor-derived memory-like NK cells functionally persist after transfer into patients with leukemia." Sci Transl Med 2022;14(633):eabm1375. PMID 35196021 / PMC9210521. NCT02782546, 15 r/r AML patients, RIC (Flu 30 mg/m2 d-6 to -2, Cy 14.5 mg/kg d-6/-5, TBI 200 cGy d-1), same-donor ML NK on day +7, N-803 10 ug/kg sc x3 weeks. Verbatim: "HLA-based NK cell tracking was not possible because the immune cells reconstituting after haplo-HCT are HLA-matched to the infused same-donor NK cells." ML NK were identified purely by mass cytometry / CITE-seq unsupervised clustering. The auditor cited Bednarski 2022 but not this — yet this is the flagship human persistence paper, and it has strictly LESS tracking than Romee 2016 (which at least had donor-vs-recipient anti-HLA mAbs). Worse, the marrow is actively producing new donor NK under an IL-15 superagonist, so "ML NK persisted >2 months" cannot be separated from "reconstituting donor NK acquired an ML-like phenotype under N-803."

(3) Adams NM, Geary CD, Santosa EK, et al. "Cytomegalovirus Infection Drives Avidity Selection of Natural Killer Cells." Immunity 2019;50:1381-1390. PMID 31103381 / PMC6614060. Ly49Hlo and Ly49Hhi splenic NK cells sorted BEFORE infection from congenically distinct WT mice and co-transferred into Klra8-/- hosts (CD45.1/CD45.2, 3-5 mice/group): "Ly49Hhi NK cells expanded more robustly and outnumbered Ly49Hlo NK cells at 7 days post infection... and preferentially contributed to the memory NK cell pool", and Ly49H levels were "clonally maintained". The authors frame it explicitly as "avidity selection". This is the NK memory field itself demonstrating that an apparent memory-differentiation phenotype is substantially SELECTION of a pre-existing subset.

(4) Grassmann S, Pachmayr LO, Leube J, et al. "Distinct Surface Expression of Activating Receptor Ly49H Drives Differential Expansion of NK Cell Clones upon Murine Cytomegalovirus Infection." Immunity 2019;50:1391-1400. PMID 31103380. Retrogenic colour-barcoding plus SINGLE-CELL adoptive transfer of Ly49H+ NK cells; clonal expansion varied enormously (up to 10,000-fold for a single clone) and the variance was predicted by PRE-EXISTING Ly49H surface density, not by anything acquired. This refutes the framing that clonal-resolution NK work is technically unavailable: the technique exists, it has been applied to NK memory, and when applied it showed bulk behaviour is driven by pre-existing clonal heterogeneity. It has simply never been pointed at CIML.

(5) Flommersfeld S, Bottcher JP, Ersching J, et al. "Fate mapping of single NK cells identifies a type 1 innate lymphoid-like lineage that bridges innate and adaptive recognition of viral infection." Immunity 2021;54:2288-2304. PMID 34437840 / PMC8528403. Verbatim: adaptive-like NK cells were "currently... thought to differentiate along a common pathway. However, by fate mapping of single NK cells upon MCMV infection, we identified two distinct NK cell lineages." Direct precedent for the canonical TWO-INDEPENDENT-ORIGINS alternative: every time single-cell fate mapping has been applied to an NK memory-differentiation claim, the single-pathway model broke.

(6) Berrien-Elliott MM, Becker-Hapak M, Cashen AF, et al. "Systemic IL-15 promotes allogeneic cell rejection in patients treated with natural killer cell adoptive therapy." Blood 2022;139:1177-1183. PMID 34797911 / PMC9211446. Across two trial cohorts, N-803/IL-15 support gave WORSE clinical activity than IL-2 because it "promot[ed] recipient CD8 T-cell activation that in turn accelerated donor NK cell rejection", and "IL-15/N-803 accelerated the ability of responding T cells to kill stimulator-derived memory-like NK cells." Persistence of infused ML NK is thus governed by host allo-rejection and the choice of exogenous cytokine, not by an intrinsic memory program — an extrinsic explanation for the persistence data the claim rests on.

SEARCHED AND NOT FOUND (0 hits each, PubMed esearch): "cytokine induced memory-like NK cell lineage tracing fate map"; "memory-like NK cell mitochondrial variant clonal"; "IL-12 IL-18 preactivated NK cell single cell transfer clone"; "cytokine induced memory-like NK cell clonal tracking barcode lentiviral"; "memory-like NK cells failure replicate negative result persistence"; "Ncr1 Cre fate mapping NK cell memory lineage tracing"; "Kaede photoconvertible NK cell tracking". I confirm the auditor's negative: no clonal-resolution CIML experiment exists in mouse or human. I also searched PubMed for "WU-NK-101 memory like NK cell acute myeloid leukemia" and found NO indexed record, so I do not cite that product as a dependency.
adv.crossfield_g4_findings:
MYELOID (trained immunity — the field CIML NK explicitly borrows from; the 2022 Front Immunol CIML review PMID 35603208 says outright that CIML NK "resemble the trained immunity observed in myeloid cells"). The myeloid field ran this exact experiment first and discovered its own fatal artefact: the long-lived "trained" peripheral cell is NOT the cell that was trained. Cirovic B et al., Cell Host Microbe 2020;28:322-334, PMID 32544459 / PMC7295478 (20 healthy volunteers, 15 BCG / 5 placebo, bone-marrow aspirates + blood at d0/d14/d90) states verbatim that HSPC reprogramming "allows for a persistent induction of a trained immunity phenotype of CD14+ monocytes, BEYOND THE INDIVIDUAL CELL'S LIFESPAN," with "BCG vaccination imprint[ing] a persistent transcriptomic myeloid bias on human HSPCs." Same conclusion from Kaufmann E et al., Cell 2018;172:176-190, PMID 29328912 ("BCG Educates Hematopoietic Stem Cells"); Khan N et al., Cell 2020;183:752-770, PMID 33125891; Kalafati L et al., Cell 2020;183:771-785, PMID 33125892. COLLISION: mouse CIML is actually protected here — Keppel 2013's Rag2-/-gc-/- hosts cannot generate new NK cells, so donor persistence out to 4 months is real. But the HUMAN CIML persistence claims are made in exactly the configuration the myeloid field showed to be uninterpretable: a marrow actively producing new donor NK cells, under IL-15 superagonist support, with NO tracking marker (Berrien-Elliott 2022 STM PMID 35196021: "HLA-based NK cell tracking was not possible"; Bednarski 2022 Blood PMID 34871371, viSNE phenotype only; Shapiro 2022 JCI PMID 35349491, "no traceable marker"). The myeloid field's answer to "is the persisting trained cell the same cell?" was NO — and human CIML has never run the equivalent control.

T CELL. Three collisions. (a) The pre-existing memory-phenotype compartment. Haluszczak C et al., J Exp Med 2009;206:435-448, PMID 19188498 / PMC2646575 showed antigen-specific memory-phenotype CD8 T cells exist in UNIMMUNIZED mice "bearing markers of homeostatic expansion"; White JT et al., Nat Commun 2016;7:11291, PMID 27097762 / PMC4844673 showed these virtual-memory cells are "15-25% of the unprimed CD8 pool", arise "in an IL-15-dependent manner", are found in human cord blood so "it was not necessary for them to be derived from antigen-experienced memory T cells", and "are capable of mediating potent immunological protection... even in the absence of their cognate antigen". The T cell field's mandatory null hypothesis for any "we induced memory" claim is therefore a pre-existing, IL-15-driven, functionally-memory compartment that was never converted. CIML NK has run no equivalent control — and Romee 2012's own marker data place the ML recall response on CD94/NKG2A/NKG2C-hi, CD57/KIR-negative less-differentiated cells, i.e. the pre-existing IL-15-responsive compartment. (b) Bulk transfer cannot license per-cell statements. Buchholz VR et al., Science 2013;340:630-635, PMID 23493420, "Disparate individual fates compose robust CD8+ T cell immunity" — single-cell fate mapping showed individual naive T cells give wildly divergent progeny, so the average behaviour of a bulk transferred population says nothing about what any cell did. Cooper 2009 (CFSE bulk), Keppel 2013 and Ni 2012 (congenic bulk) are all bulk transfers. (c) The mechanism collision. Cooper's own ref 21, Bird JJ et al., Immunity 1998;9:229-237, established that Th1 IFN-gamma competence is acquired THROUGH cell division via epigenetic remodelling. Cooper 2009 Fig 4 finds the opposite in NK — generation 0 (never divided) equals generations 1-3 — and the authors state the contrast explicitly ("This aspect is in contrast to CD4+ T cells"). Read against the T cell field, a division-independent, dose/duration-graded (5 h weaker than overnight), decay-prone effect is the signature of persistent PRIMING (a long-lived signalling/protein state), not of differentiation; Cooper concedes the alternative in print ("Alternatively, an increased activation time may allow for a higher percentage of NK cells to differentiate into memory-like cells"), and Keppel 2013 concedes "these enhanced responses could represent a residual priming effect, rather than a memory-like response."

ILC. (a) The ILC memory literature has the survival-selection artefact written into its own model: Martinez-Gonzalez I et al., Immunity 2016;45:198-208, PMID 27421705 — ILC2s "proliferated and secreted cytokines upon initial stimulation with allergen or IL-33, and this phase was followed by a CONTRACTION PHASE... Some ILC2s persisted long after the resolution of the inflammation as allergen-experienced ILC2s and responded to unrelated allergens more potently than naive ILC2s." The memory-like cells are by construction the SURVIVORS of a die-off — the same structure Terren 2023 (PMID 37575238) documents for IL-12/15/18-treated NK, i.e. the preactivation step is a survival filter. Same experimental design as CIML (bulk transfer + heterologous recall assay), same unexcluded alternative. (b) The ILC field's methodological standard is stricter than the NK field's: apparent ILC3->ILC1 conversion (e.g. Mucosal Immunol 2021, PMID 33214656; c-Maf, J Exp Med 2020, PMID 31570496) is adjudicated with genetic fate-mapping reporters, not marker overlap or transfer. (c) The single most relevant ILC result sits on the NK/ILC1 boundary: Flommersfeld 2021 Immunity, PMID 34437840, single-NK-cell fate mapping split what the field assumed was one adaptive-like NK differentiation pathway into a cNK lineage and an ILC1-like lineage. NET BEARING ON P2: all three fields independently converged on the same rule — a "memory-like" state defined by a bulk recall assay plus a persistence timecourse is NOT adjudicable without either (i) single-cell/clonal fate mapping, or (ii) a host that provably cannot generate the cell de novo. Mouse CIML satisfies (ii) only (Keppel 2013). Human CIML satisfies neither.

adv.load_bearing_reason:
HIGH is correct, but the auditor located the load in the wrong place and was generous about part of it. WHAT IS NOT LOAD-BEARING: the CAR-ML-NK product line the auditor leaned on — Gang 2020 Blood PMID 32614951 (CD19-CAR ML NK), Dong 2022 PNAS PMID 35696582 (NPM1c-neoepitope CAR ML NK), Sci Adv 2024 PMID 38996027 (mesothelin CAR ML NK, both PMIDs verified in PubMed) — depends only on the EMPIRICAL manufacturing fact that 16 h IL-12/15/18 exposure yields more potent NK cells. That fact is robustly replicated and survives intact whether the mechanism is conversion or selection of a pre-existing subset. Listing those three as dependencies of the LINEAGE claim overstates the load. I also could not find any PubMed-indexed record for WU-NK-101, so I decline to cite it as a dependency (searched, not found).

WHAT IS GENUINELY LOAD-BEARING, and enough on its own for HIGH: the PERSISTENCE / "differentiated memory state" sub-claim, which drives trial design, dosing schedule and product definition. The single most concrete named dependency is Berrien-Elliott MM, Foltz JA, Russler-Germain DA, et al., "Hematopoietic cell transplantation donor-derived memory-like NK cells functionally persist after transfer into patients with leukemia," Sci Transl Med 2022;14(633):eabm1375, PMID 35196021 / PMC9210521, trial NCT02782546: 15 relapsed/refractory AML patients, RIC haplo-HCT augmented with a SINGLE same-donor ML NK infusion on day +7 plus 3 weeks of N-803, 87% composite complete response at day +28 including clearance of TP53 variants. Its central biological conclusion — "ML NK cells persisted for over 2 months" and are "distinct from conventional NK cells" — is derived entirely from unsupervised mass-cytometry/CITE-seq clustering, because the authors themselves state "HLA-based NK cell tracking was not possible because the immune cells reconstituting after haplo-HCT are HLA-matched to the infused same-donor NK cells." If the ML state is instead a phenotype that graft-derived donor NK cells acquire under N-803, or a selected pre-existing CD56bright-like subset, that persistence conclusion collapses and with it the rationale for a one-shot day+7 infusion rather than repeat dosing. Three further real dependencies: Bednarski 2022 Blood PMID 34871371 (pediatric post-transplant AML; "persisting ML NK cells" at 3-6 months by viSNE phenotype alone); Shapiro 2022 JCI PMID 35349491 (which already concedes "there was no traceable marker in the infused CIML NK cells"); and the first-in-human ML NK + N-803 + CTLA-4 blockade trial in advanced head and neck cancer, J Hematol Oncol 2025, PMID 39948608 (verified) — a solid-tumour indication justified by the durability of the ML state, not by acute potency. Finally, the field is ALREADY re-engineering on the basis of this claim: Berrien-Elliott 2022 Blood PMID 34797911 switched cytokine support away from N-803 toward IL-2 explicitly to protect infused "memory-like NK cells" from host CD8 allo-rejection — a persistence-driven design decision. If the operative mechanism is instead CD25 installation plus exogenous IL-2 (Leong 2014, PMID 24434782) acting on a pre-existing responsive subset, the correct optimisation target shifts from "how long/strong to preactivate" to "which subset to sort and how to dose IL-2" — a materially different product.
adv.better_primary_source: NONE — the audit identified the primary-source chain correctly, and I verified it independently: Cooper 2009 PNAS (PMID 19181844, PMC2644138) is the term-coining mouse origin and did NOT use the triple (IL-12 10 ng/mL + IL-18 50 ng/mL with low-dose IL-15 10 ng/mL as a survival factor, shown dispensable at 5 h), and Romee 2012 Blood (PMID 22983442, PMC3520618) is the true earliest primary source for the IL-12/IL-15/IL-18 TRIPLE named in claim P2 ("preactivated for 16 hours using rhIL-12 (10 ng/mL) + rhIL-18 (50 ng/mL) + rhIL-15 (1 ng/mL)"), human, and — confirmed from its Methods — with no in vivo arm whatsoever ("Currently, we are evaluating in vivo xenograft approaches in NOD-SCID-gc-/- mice"). Keppel 2013 (PMID 23530145) remains the strongest transfer experiment. HOWEVER the audit's EVIDENCE SET is incomplete in one important respect that changes the human verdict: it omits Berrien-Elliott MM et al., Sci Transl Med 2022;14:eabm1375, PMID 35196021 / PMC9210521, which is now the field's flagship human persistence paper (NCT02782546, 15 patients) and which has strictly weaker in vivo tracking than Romee 2016 — no HLA discrimination at all, by the authors' own statement. Any registry row for P2 should carry 35196021 alongside 27655849. It also omits Leong 2014 (PMID 24434782 / PMC3959288), which is the mechanistic key to the human in vivo expansion data.
